Question 24 [7 marks]: Discuss the effectiveness of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 7):
7 marks: Provides informed arguments for AND/OR against the effectiveness of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights | Demonstrates a thorough understanding of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights
5–6 marks: Provides arguments for AND/OR against the effectiveness of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights | Demonstrates a sound understanding of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights
3–4 marks: Attempts to provide arguments for AND/OR against the effectiveness of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights | Demonstrates an understanding of Australian legal responses in enforcing human rights
1–2 marks: Makes general statements about Australian legal responses AND/OR human rights | May provide an example

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
A number of important human rights have been protected in Australia, although their enforceability varies. For instance, there are explicit rights contained in the Australian Constitution such as the right to vote in Commonwealth elections (s. 41). Similarly, statute law has contributed to the enforcement of human rights through the application of legislation such as the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 (Cth). Common law also reveals how Australia responds and enforces human rights, such as Dietrich v The Queen 1992. The High Court of Australia recognised the importance of a fair trial if the accused represents themselves or has an unqualified person representing them. This right, however, does not automatically allow the accused to acquire legal assistance if they did not meet the criteria for legal aid.
The Australian Human Rights Commission (AHRC) was establised by the AHRC Act 1986 (Cth). However, this legislation, while establishing the statutory authority, may not lead to binding or enforceable judgements. Some Australian responses to the implementation of international law can also limit the enforcement of human rights. This can be seen with Australia’s interpretation of the Refugee Convention 1951 (UN) through the Migration Act 1958 (Cth).
